title: The ocean's temperature by depth
what: The ocean's temperature each month since January 1940 at three depths, the surface, 100 m and 700 m, against the same calendar month's mean over 1991–2020, from IAP v4.2's gridded temperature (Cheng et al. 2024). Blue is colder than usual for the month and red warmer, to ±4 °C at the surface and 100 m and ±1 °C at 700 m. At 100 m El Niño shows best: the warm water of the western Pacific slides east along the equator and the thermocline deepens off South America. Below, four deep levels, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 and 5,000 m, a map a year since 1940 against the 1991–2020 mean of the yearly means, to ±0.2 °C at 2,000 m down to ±0.1 °C at 4,000 and 5,000 m: the deep ocean warms by hundredths of a degree a decade, slowest at the bottom.
how: IAP gives each month's temperature anomaly for each 1° cell at 119 depths; the site takes the three, measures each against its calendar month's 1991–2020 mean (IAP's own anomalies are against another period), averages them onto the site's 1° grid and rounds them to 0.1 °C (0.025 °C at 700 m), finer than the deep ocean was measured. The last month there is stands for the months since, said so. At the deep levels each year is the mean of its twelve months, kept where all twelve have a value, rounded to 0.005 °C (0.0025 °C at 4,000 and 5,000 m); the deep ocean changes too slowly for monthly maps to differ. IAP's 6,000 m level holds no values, and 5,000 m only the deep basins.
others: Before the Argo floats (from about 2005) the deep ocean, and before about 1960 much of the ocean at any depth, was sparsely measured: IAP fills the gaps from climate models' covariances, so the early maps and the deep ones lean on that filling. The surface here is IAP's 1 m level, not the satellite and ship blend of the El Niño layer's sea surface maps (OISST), so the two differ a little. Below 2,000 m, where Argo floats do not reach, the ocean is measured by research ships along a few repeated lines about once a decade, and since the mid 2010s by a few Deep Argo floats: the deep maps are IAP's reconstruction more than measurements, in every year.
